*   If I rank y first, I am guaranteed to get y since I have priority 1 there.
*   If I rank w first, I am guaranteed to get w since I have priority 1 there.

Since I prefer x > z > y > w, I should start by considering x and z. Given the popularity of y, it is likely that many students will apply to y. This might mean that x and z are less competitive.

My priority at x and z is the same (2). However, I prefer x to z. Therefore, I should rank x higher than z.

If I rank x first, and I get rejected, where should I go next? Since I prefer z > y > w, I should consider z. If I get rejected from z, I would want to go to y or w. Since y > w, I should consider y.

Therefore, my ranking should be x > z > y > w.
